note: Contracts with el: de + el = del.

ex.en: This coffee is from Colombia.

ex.es: Es el carro de mi hermano.
ex.en: It's my brother's car.

ex.es: Quiero un vaso de agua, por favor.
ex.en: I'd like a glass of water, please.
I'm already at the office.

ex.es: Nos vemos en el parque a las cinco.
ex.en: See you at the park at five.

ex.es: Mis llaves están en la mesa.
ex.en: My keys are on the table.

note: Contracts with el: a + el = al. Also marks people: veo a Ana.

ex.es: Le di el libro a Kevin.
ex.en: I gave the book to Kevin.

ex.es: Voy a ir con mi primo.
ex.en: I'm going to go with my cousin.
On Friday I'm going to Monterrey.

note: Before a masculine noun: un (un libro); feminine: una (una casa).

ex.en: I'd like a coffee with milk.

ex.es: Tengo una hermana y dos hermanos.
ex.en: I have one sister and two brothers.
I only want one, thanks.

note: The question word 'what?' takes an accent: ¿qué? tener que = to have to.

ex.en: I think it's going to rain.

ex.es: Mi hermano es más alto que yo.
ex.en: My brother is taller than me.
I have to work on Saturday.

note: Goes right before the verb: no tengo.

ex.en: I'm not hungry yet.

ex.es: Hoy no puedo ir, lo siento.
ex.en: I can't go today, sorry.
No, thanks, I already ate a lot.

note: por vs. para is tricky: gracias por = thanks for; por la tarde = in the afternoon.

ex.en: Thanks a lot for your help.

ex.es: Te llamo mañana por la tarde.
ex.en: I'll call you tomorrow afternoon.

ex.es: Caminamos por el parque después de comer.
ex.en: We walked through the park after eating.

note: With me / with you: conmigo, contigo.

ex.es: Vivo con mi esposa y mi perro.
ex.en: I live with my wife and my dog.

ex.es: Un taco con todo, por favor.
ex.en: A taco with everything, please.
I talked with the doctor yesterday.

note: Plural: sus. Also 'your' when you speak to someone as usted.

ex.es: Ana dejó su teléfono en casa.
ex.en: Ana left her phone at home.
The neighbors are selling their car.
Sir, is this your seat?

note: para + infinitive = in order to: para hablar.

ex.en: This gift is for you.

ex.es: Estudio español para hablar con mis pacientes.
ex.en: I study Spanish to talk with my patients.
I need a table for four.

note: Learn hay = there is/are; había = there was/were. Also helper verb: he comido.

ex.en: Is there a bathroom around here?

ex.es: No hay leche en el refrigerador.
ex.en: There's no milk in the fridge.

ex.es: Había mucha gente en la fiesta.
ex.en: There were a lot of people at the party.

note: Feminine: esta; plural: estos, estas. Don't confuse esta (this) with está (is).

ex.en: This restaurant is very good.
Can I try on this shirt?

ex.es: Este fin de semana voy a descansar.
ex.en: This weekend I'm going to rest.

note: Also for age and feelings: tener 30 años, tener hambre. tener que = have to.

ex.es: Tengo dos hijos y una hija.
ex.en: I have two sons and a daughter.

ex.es: ¿Tienes hambre? Hay pizza en la cocina.
ex.en: Are you hungry? There's pizza in the kitchen.
My grandmother is eighty years old.

note: The question word 'how?' takes an accent: ¿cómo?

ex.es: Mi hijo es alto como su papá.
ex.en: My son is tall like his dad.

ex.es: Trabajo como enfermera en un hospital.
ex.en: I work as a nurse at a hospital.

ex.es: Como es tarde, voy a tomar un taxi.
ex.en: Since it's late, I'm going to take a taxi.

note: Always with an accent. más ... que = more ... than.

ex.en: Do you want more coffee or tea?
This hotel is cheaper.

ex.es: Mi hermana es la más alta de la familia.
ex.en: My sister is the tallest in the family.

note: Goes before a conjugated verb: me llamó. Attached to commands: llámame.

ex.en: Can you pass me the salt, please?
My boss called me yesterday.

ex.es: Hoy me duele mucho la cabeza.
ex.en: My head hurts a lot today.

note: Weather: hace frío, hace calor. Past: hice, hizo.

ex.en: What are you going to do on Saturday?
It's really hot out today.

ex.es: Mi esposa hizo la cena anoche.
ex.en: My wife made dinner last night.

note: Stem changes: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden.

ex.en: Can you help me with this?

ex.es: No puedo ir a la fiesta.
ex.en: I can't go to the party.
Can I pay by card here?

note: No accent. With an accent, sí means 'yes'.

ex.es: Si llueve, nos quedamos en casa.
ex.en: If it rains, we'll stay home.

ex.es: Avísame si vas a llegar tarde.
ex.en: Let me know if you're going to be late.

ex.es: No sé si tengo tiempo hoy.
ex.en: I don't know if I have time today.

note: Very irregular: voy, vas, va, vamos, van; past fui. ir a + infinitive = going to.

ex.es: Mañana voy al mercado con Sofía.
ex.en: Tomorrow I'm going to the market with Sofía.

ex.es: ¿Fuiste a la playa el verano pasado?
ex.en: Did you go to the beach last summer?

ex.es: Prefiero ir al trabajo en metro.
ex.en: I'd rather go to work by subway.

note: Feminine: toda. todos los días = every day. todo el mundo = everyone.

ex.en: I ate the whole cake.

ex.es: Todos mis amigos van a venir.
ex.en: All my friends are going to come.
Is everything okay at work?

note: Object form of tú. té with an accent means 'tea'.

ex.en: I'll call you later, okay?
Do you like Mexican food?
My mom says hi to you.

note: Becomes u before a word starting with o-: siete u ocho.

ex.en: Would you prefer water, milk, or beer?

ex.es: Ana llega el lunes o el martes.
ex.en: Ana arrives on Monday or Tuesday.

ex.es: ¿La casa es tuya o es rentada?
ex.en: Is the house yours, or is it rented?

note: Plural: mis. With an accent, mí means 'me' after a preposition: para mí.

ex.es: Mi casa está cerca del parque.
ex.en: My house is near the park.
This is my wife.

ex.es: Perdí mi teléfono en el taxi.
ex.en: I lost my phone in the taxi.

note: Present: veo, ves, ve. Past: vi, viste, vio. Nos vemos = see you.

ex.en: Do you want to watch a movie today?

ex.es: Te veo mañana en la escuela.
ex.en: I'll see you tomorrow at school.

ex.es: Ayer vi a Diego en el súper.
ex.en: Yesterday I saw Diego at the supermarket.

note: Feminine: esa; plural: esos, esas.

ex.en: How much is that black watch?
That movie was really good.
Who's that man in blue?

note: te quiero = I love you (family, partner, close friends).

ex.en: I want a really cold beer.
Do you want to go for a walk tomorrow?
I love you so much, Mom, take care.

note: Always write the ñ: 'ano' is a different, rude word.

ex.en: How old is your daughter?

ex.es: El año pasado fuimos a Perú.
ex.en: Last year we went to Peru.
Happy New Year, everyone!

note: No accent. With an accent, tú means 'you'. Plural: tus.

ex.en: What's your phone number?
I like your new shirt.
And how's your mom doing?

note: Often left out because the verb already shows the person: (yo) tengo.

ex.en: I'll pay the bill today.
I'm from Chicago, and you?

ex.es: Ella cocina y yo lavo los platos.
ex.en: She cooks and I wash the dishes.

note: Feminine: otra. Never 'un otro': otro café = another coffee.

ex.en: Could you bring me another coffee, please?

ex.es: Me gusta más el otro color.
ex.en: I like the other color better.

ex.es: Hoy no puedo, mejor otro día.
ex.en: I can't today; let's do another day.

ex.es: Un café sin azúcar, por favor.
ex.en: A coffee without sugar, please.

ex.es: Salí sin paraguas y me mojé.
ex.en: I went out without an umbrella and got wet.

ex.es: No puedo vivir sin mi celular.
ex.en: I can't live without my cell phone.

note: The question word takes an accent: ¿cuándo? About the future it takes the subjunctive: cuando llegues.

ex.es: Mándame un mensaje cuando llegues a casa.
ex.en: Text me when you get home.

ex.es: Cuando era niño, vivía en Texas.
ex.en: When I was a kid, I lived in Texas.

ex.es: Me pongo nervioso cuando hablo en público.
ex.en: I get nervous when I speak in public.

note: Used before adjectives and adverbs; for 'very much' use mucho.

ex.en: The food is really good.
I'm very tired today.
Their house is very big.

note: For people and places use conocer. Present: sé, sabes, sabe.

ex.es: No sé dónde está el baño.
ex.en: I don't know where the bathroom is.
Do you know if there's a pharmacy nearby?
My son can already read.

note: Masculine even though it ends in -a: el día, buenos días.

ex.en: Good morning, how are you?
I work eight hours a day.
What day is your birthday?

note: Always with an accent. así es = that's right.

ex.en: Should I cut it like this or smaller?
Oh well, that's life.
Why are you talking to me like that?

note: Feminine: nuestra; plural: nuestros, nuestras.

ex.es: Nuestro vuelo sale a las seis.
ex.en: Our flight leaves at six.
Welcome, this is our home.

ex.es: Nuestros hijos van a la misma escuela.
ex.en: Our kids go to the same school.

note: Never followed by a noun: ¿Qué es eso? por eso = that's why.

ex.en: What's that you're eating?
That sounds good to me.

ex.es: Por eso llegué tarde al trabajo.
ex.en: That's why I got to work late.

note: deber + infinitive = should: debes descansar.

ex.es: Debes dormir más, te ves cansado.
ex.en: You should sleep more; you look tired.
Excuse me, how much do I owe you?

ex.es: Los niños deben estar en la cama a las nueve.
ex.en: The kids should be in bed at nine.

ex.es: Tengo dos perros y un gato.
ex.en: I have two dogs and a cat.

ex.es: Dos tacos de pollo, por favor.
ex.en: Two chicken tacos, please.
See you in two hours.

note: An adverb: hablas bien. For 'good' before a noun use bueno.

ex.en: I'm fine, thanks, and you?
You speak Spanish very well.
Did you sleep well at the hotel?

note: desde hace = for (a length of time): desde hace tres años.

ex.en: I've lived in Chicago since 2020.
I'm calling you from the airport.

ex.es: Desde mi ventana veo el lago.
ex.en: From my window I can see the lake.

en: until; up to; as far as
note: hasta luego = see you later; hasta mañana = see you tomorrow.

ex.en: Okay, I'm leaving. See you tomorrow!

ex.es: La tienda abre hasta las nueve.
ex.en: The store is open until nine.

ex.es: Caminamos hasta la playa desde el hotel.
ex.en: We walked all the way to the beach from the hotel.

en: to happen; to pass; to spend (time)
note: ¿Qué pasó? = What happened? In Mexico, ¡pásale! = come in.

ex.en: What happened to your hand?

ex.es: Pasamos el fin de semana en la playa.
ex.en: We spent the weekend at the beach.

ex.es: El autobús pasa cada diez minutos.
ex.en: The bus comes by every ten minutes.

note: Never followed by a noun: ¿Qué es esto? Don't confuse with estoy (I am).

ex.en: Can you tell me how much this costs?
Mmm, this is really tasty.
I don't understand this; can you help me?

note: In Mexico, ahorita = right now (or soon, loosely).

ex.en: I can't right now; I'm driving.
So where do you live now, Minho?

ex.es: Mi hija ahora trabaja en un banco.
ex.en: My daughter works at a bank now.

note: dejar de + infinitive = to stop doing: dejar de fumar.

ex.es: Dejé las llaves en el carro.
ex.en: I left the keys in the car.

ex.es: Mis papás no me dejan salir.
ex.en: My parents don't let me go out.

ex.es: Mi papá quiere dejar de fumar.
ex.en: My dad wants to quit smoking.

note: Always feminine, even for a man: es una persona amable.

ex.en: She's a very kind person.
How many people are coming to the party?

ex.es: El boleto cuesta veinte dólares por persona.
ex.en: The ticket costs twenty dollars per person.
I need to tell you something.
Where can I put my things?

ex.es: Compré muchas cosas en el mercado.
ex.en: I bought a lot of things at the market.

note: For clock time use la hora; for 'one time' use la vez.

ex.en: I don't have time to eat breakfast.

ex.es: Hace mucho tiempo que no te veo.
ex.en: I haven't seen you in a long time.
What's the weather going to be like tomorrow?

note: No accent in statements; questions use ¿dónde?

ex.es: Esa es la casa donde crecí.
ex.en: That's the house where I grew up.

ex.es: El restaurante donde comimos estaba buenísimo.
ex.en: The restaurant where we ate was amazing.

ex.es: Vamos al parque donde jugábamos de niños.
ex.en: Let's go to the park where we played as kids.

note: Agrees with the noun: mucha gente, muchos amigos. As an adverb it doesn't change.

ex.en: I really like your house.
There's a lot of traffic today.

ex.es: Tengo muchas preguntas para el doctor.
ex.en: I have a lot of questions for the doctor.

note: algo más = anything else.

ex.en: Do you want to eat something before we go?
Can I help you with anything else?

ex.es: Creo que algo está mal con mi carro.
ex.en: I think something's wrong with my car.

note: hablar con = to talk with; hablar de = to talk about.

ex.en: My grandparents only speak Spanish.

ex.es: Hablé con Ana por teléfono anoche.
ex.en: I talked to Ana on the phone last night.
Can you speak more slowly, please?

note: As 'alone' it agrees: sola, solos. Older spelling for 'only': sólo.

ex.en: I only have ten dollars.
My son only eats pizza.
I live alone in an apartment.

ex.es: Mi vida cambió mucho este año.
ex.en: My life changed a lot this year.

ex.es: Toda mi vida he vivido en Chicago.
ex.en: I've lived in Chicago my whole life.

ex.es: La vida en la ciudad es cara.
ex.en: Life in the city is expensive.

note: Irregular: pongo; past puse; command pon. ponerse = to put on (clothes).

ex.en: Where do I put the grocery bags?

ex.es: Puse la leche en el refrigerador.
ex.en: I put the milk in the fridge.

ex.es: Pon la tele, ya empieza el partido.
ex.en: Turn on the TV; the game is starting.

note: tan ... como = as ... as: tan alto como yo.

ex.en: Your daughter is so big!

ex.es: No es tan caro como pensaba.
ex.en: It's not as expensive as I thought.
Why did you get here so late?

note: A nation. For 'the countryside' use el campo.

ex.en: What country are you from?

ex.es: México es un país muy bonito.
ex.en: Mexico is a very beautiful country.

ex.es: Quiero visitar otro país el próximo año.
ex.en: I want to visit another country next year.

en: to be left; to be located; to fit
note: quedarse = to stay: me quedo en casa. te queda bien = it suits you.

ex.es: Ya no queda café, voy a comprar más.
ex.en: There's no coffee left; I'm going to buy more.
Excuse me, where is the bank?

ex.es: Esa camisa te queda muy bien.
ex.en: That shirt looks really good on you.

note: Never changes form: cada día, cada semana.

ex.en: I go to the gym every morning.
Everyone pays for their own.

ex.es: Tomo una pastilla cada ocho horas.
ex.en: I take a pill every eight hours.

note: For an all-female group: ellas.

ex.en: They live near us.
Are they coming to dinner?

ex.es: Ellas son mis compañeras de trabajo.
ex.en: They're my coworkers.

note: ¿Qué te parece? = What do you think? parecerse a = to look like (someone).

ex.en: What do you think of my idea?
It looks like it's going to rain.

ex.es: Tu hijo se parece mucho a ti.
ex.en: Your son looks a lot like you.

note: Stem change: pienso, piensas. pensar en = to think about.

ex.en: What do you think of the movie?

ex.es: Estoy pensando en ti, mi amor.
ex.en: I'm thinking about you, my love.
I think it's a good idea.

note: Also 'room, space': no hay lugar = there's no room.

ex.en: This place is very quiet.
Do you know a good place to eat?
There's no place to park.

note: Same spelling as trabajo = I work.

ex.es: Salgo del trabajo a las cinco.
ex.en: I get off work at five.
My brother is looking for a job.

ex.es: El trabajo de mi esposa es muy estresante.
ex.en: My wife's job is very stressful.

note: muchas gracias = thank you very much. gracias por = thanks for.

ex.es: Gracias por venir a mi fiesta.
ex.en: Thanks for coming to my party.
Thank you, you're very kind.

ex.es: Le mandé un mensaje para darle las gracias.
ex.en: I sent her a message to thank her.

note: Telling time: las cinco menos diez = ten to five.

ex.en: It's ten to five.

ex.es: Quiero comer menos azúcar este año.
ex.en: I want to eat less sugar this year.

ex.es: Este celular cuesta menos que el otro.
ex.en: This cell phone costs less than the other one.

note: mi mujer = my wife (casual); mi esposa is more formal.

ex.en: That woman is my boss.
There's a woman waiting for you outside.

ex.es: Mi mujer cocina mejor que yo.
ex.en: My wife cooks better than I do.

note: en casa = at home; a casa = (to) home.

ex.en: I'm staying home today.

ex.es: Su casa tiene un jardín enorme.
ex.en: Their house has a huge yard.
What time do you get home?

ex.es: Ese hombre es el dueño del restaurante.
ex.en: That man is the owner of the restaurant.

ex.es: El baño de hombres está allá.
ex.en: The men's bathroom is over there.

ex.es: Mi hijo ya es todo un hombre.
ex.en: My son is a grown man now.

note: Always with an accent. por aquí = around here.

ex.es: Ven aquí un momento, por favor.
ex.en: Come here for a moment, please.
Here's your change, sir.

ex.es: Vivo aquí desde hace tres años.
ex.en: I've lived here for three years.

note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene; past vine. Ven = come (command).

ex.en: Are you coming to the party on Saturday?

ex.es: Mi mamá viene a visitarnos en diciembre.
ex.en: My mom is coming to visit us in December.

ex.es: Hoy vine al trabajo en bici.
ex.en: Today I came to work by bike.

note: In Latin America, tomar is the everyday verb for drinking.

ex.en: Let's go have a coffee.
I took a taxi to the airport.
Take this pill with water.

note: Feminine: última. la última vez = the last time.

ex.es: ¿A qué hora sale el último tren?
ex.en: What time does the last train leave?

ex.es: La última vez que fui, estaba cerrado.
ex.en: The last time I went, it was closed.
Did you see the latest episode?

note: de acuerdo = okay, agreed; estoy de acuerdo = I agree.

ex.en: I agree with you.

ex.es: De acuerdo, nos vemos a las ocho.
ex.en: Okay, see you at eight.

ex.es: Llegamos a un acuerdo con el dueño.
ex.en: We reached an agreement with the owner.
I love this city.
What city do you live in?

ex.es: El centro de la ciudad tiene mucho tráfico.
ex.en: Downtown has a lot of traffic.

note: en este momento = right now. Un momento = just a moment.

ex.es: Un momento, por favor, ya vengo.
ex.en: One moment, please; I'll be right back.

ex.es: En este momento no puedo hablar.
ex.en: I can't talk right now.

ex.es: Fue el mejor momento del viaje.
ex.en: It was the best moment of the trip.

note: la hija = daughter. los hijos = children (sons and daughters).

ex.es: Mi hijo juega fútbol los sábados.
ex.en: My son plays soccer on Saturdays.
How many kids do you have?
My daughter studies medicine.

note: Masculine even though it ends in -a: el problema. No hay problema = no problem.

ex.es: No hay ningún problema, de verdad.
ex.en: It's no problem at all, really.

ex.es: Tengo un problema con mi computadora.
ex.en: I have a problem with my computer.

ex.es: El problema es que no tengo dinero.
ex.en: The problem is that I don't have money.

note: A female friend: la amiga.

ex.en: He's my best friend.

ex.es: Voy a cenar con unos amigos.
ex.en: I'm going to have dinner with some friends.

ex.es: Mi amiga Sofía vive en Bogotá.
ex.en: My friend Sofía lives in Bogotá.

note: For facts use saber. Present: conozco. conocer a + person.

ex.en: Do you know my sister?
Nice to meet you, ma'am.
I still haven't been to Guadalajara.

ex.es: ¿En qué parte de la ciudad vives?
ex.en: What part of the city do you live in?
My parents live in Texas.
I lived in Peru for two years.

note: With an accent. Without it, el means 'the'.

ex.en: He's my husband, Diego.
I'm going to the movies with him.
Does he work at the hospital too?

note: ¿Qué hora es? = What time is it? For time in general use el tiempo.

ex.en: Excuse me, what time is it?
What time does the movie start?

ex.es: Llevo una hora esperando el autobús.
ex.en: I've been waiting for the bus for an hour.

note: Plural: ellas.

ex.es: Ella es mi compañera de cuarto.
ex.en: She's my roommate.

ex.es: Ayer hablé con ella por teléfono.
ex.en: I talked to her on the phone yesterday.
Does she know you're coming?
I need to go to the bathroom.
Do you need help with the bags?
We need to buy milk and eggs.

note: lo siento = I'm sorry. sentirse + adjective: me siento bien.

ex.en: Sorry, I'm late.
How are you feeling today?

ex.es: Siento que algo no está bien.
ex.en: I feel like something isn't right.
Today is my birthday.
What are we going to eat today?
The pharmacy is closed today.

note: Negative: nadie = no one.

ex.en: Does anyone want more cake?
Someone called you a while ago.
Is anyone home?
I have three older brothers.
I'll be there in three minutes.
That's three dollars and fifty cents.

note: un poco = a little: un poco de agua.

ex.en: I speak a little Spanish.

ex.es: Espera un poco, ya casi termino.
ex.en: Wait a bit; I'm almost done.
My son eats very little.

note: llamarse = to be called: me llamo Ana = my name is Ana.

ex.en: I'll call you tonight.
Hi, what's your name?

ex.es: Llamé al doctor para hacer una cita.
ex.en: I called the doctor to make an appointment.
Can I use your bathroom?
I wear glasses to drive.
How do you use this machine?

note: Last name: el apellido.

ex.en: What's your name, ma'am?

ex.es: No me acuerdo de su nombre.
ex.en: I don't remember his name.
Write your name here.

note: Stem change: entiendo, entiendes, entiende.

ex.en: I don't understand; can you repeat that?
Did you understand what the teacher said?

ex.es: Mi abuela no entiende su celular.
ex.en: My grandma can't figure out her cell phone.

note: Plural: meses.

ex.en: I pay the rent every month.

ex.es: El próximo mes vamos a Cancún.
ex.en: Next month we're going to Cancún.
My baby is three months old.
And what do you do for work?
I work at a hospital.

ex.es: Mi esposa trabajó toda la noche.
ex.en: My wife worked all night.

note: buenas noches = good evening / good night. esta noche = tonight.

ex.en: Good night, sleep well.
I'm working nights this week.
What are we doing tonight?
